aggressive_definition: Aggressive prostate cancer defined as Stage III/IV or Gleason score ≥8; non-aggressive disease was Stage II and Gleason score <8.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: Cases were classified on cancer stage and severity into 619 non-aggressive (Stage II and Gleason score <8) and 328 aggressive cases (Stage III/IV or Gleason score ≥8).
reason: The study evaluated prostate cancer risk among 947 cases and separately analyzed incident aggressive and non-aggressive case groups. The aggressive endpoint was explicitly defined by stage or Gleason score.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Current alcohol intake did not increase prostate cancer risk but lifetime intake increased risk for both non-aggressive and aggressive cases, with an odds ratio of 1.78 (95 % CI 1.19-2.66) and 2.00 (95 % CI 1.19-3.36), respectively, for the highest intake quartile compared to non-drinkers with evidence for a linear trend.
estimate_classifications.reason: The ordering indicated by “respectively” assigns OR 1.78 to non-aggressive prostate cancer and OR 2.00 to aggressive prostate cancer. Therefore, the supplied 1.78 estimate is nonaggressive, not general or aggressive.
